task: WG-LFM-1 follow-up — MEASURE the gemma4 enable_thinking toggle
not_decision_grade_because: host uptime exceeds the 7 d constitutional limit
CPU scope is ONE region (q0 = cores 0-23, membind 0, -t 24), not the canonical full-machine 0-95 / -t 96 recipe
n=5 prompts, n=2 repeats; no tool-schema or repair-rate measurement
raw-completion harness, not a served llama-server; gemma4 MTP self-speculation (draft_max=2) is NOT exercised, so gemma's t/s here is base decode only and production would be faster
question: worker_general (gemma4-26B-A4B) runs with enable_thinking=false. The 2026-08-12 scout benched every arm with thinking ON. How many tokens does the incumbent actually emit under the production setting, and does it stay correct?

method.why_not_a_server: enable_thinking is a chat-template kwarg applied at render time. The prompt was rendered here from the GGUF-embedded template and fed to llama-completion in RAW mode (-no-cnv), so the exact production prompt string is what gets tokenized. No process lifecycle.
method.render: jinja2 3.1.6, context = {messages, bos_token:'', eos_token, add_generation_prompt:true, enable_thinking} — the same keys common/chat.cpp:common_chat_template_direct_apply_impl puts in the jinja context (chat.cpp:891-896).
method.bos: bos_token rendered EMPTY because tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token=true; llama-completion's common_tokenize(..., add_special=true, parse_special=true) prepends <bos> itself.
method.token_counting: real tokenizer only — llama-tokenize for prompt tokens, llama-completion's common_perf_print eval-runs for generated tokens. No chars/4 proxy.

cpu_scope.region_lock: held via epyc-orchestrator/scripts/region-lock for every run, released after

toggle_is_real.verdict: YES — enable_thinking is wired into the gemma4 template and changes the rendered prompt

mechanism.line_179_182: enable_thinking=true opens a system turn and injects the '<|think|>' marker
mechanism.line_359_360: if NOT enable_thinking, the generation prompt appends '<|channel>thought\n<channel|>' — an immediately-CLOSED, EMPTY thought channel. Suppression is a prefill, not a system instruction.
mechanism.default: 'not enable_thinking | default(false)' — with the kwarg absent the template DEFAULTS TO SUPPRESSED. llama.cpp overrides that: common/chat.h:261 sets enable_thinking=true, which is why the scout (no flag) got thinking.

controls: llama-completion --jinja -st (llama.cpp applies the template ITSELF, default enable_thinking=true) produced a prompt token-for-token IDENTICAL to the hand-rendered think_on prompt (31 tokens). The hand render is therefore llama.cpp's render.

thinking-ON reasoning text reproduces the 2026-08-12 scout: q1 and q5 byte-identical, q2/q3/q4 same structure with minor wording drift (llama-cli's embedded-server decode path vs llama-completion; my own harness is bit-reproducible across repeats).
repeat run: gen-token counts identical in both conditions (see *_rep2).

production_path_verified.registry: orchestration/derived/stack_priors.yaml roles.worker_general.acceleration.enable_thinking=false, thinking_control={mode: reasoning_off, source: reasoning}; serving.launch.runtime.flags.reasoning='off' (also toolrunner, worker_explore, worker_math — all four gemma4 roles).
production_path_verified.server: llama-server --reasoning off -> params_base.enable_reasoning=0 -> server-context.cpp:1463 enable_thinking=false -> server-common.cpp:1064 inputs.enable_thinking -> chat.cpp:895 jinja context. The served render is the think_off render measured here.
production_path_verified.cli_caveat: llama-completion IGNORES -rea off (default_template_kwargs is consumed only by common_chat_format_example in that tool) — verified: -rea off still rendered 31 tokens. This is a CLI-tool gap, not a serving gap; do not use llama-cli/llama-completion -rea to reproduce production thinking state.

correctness_thinking_off.verdict: 5/5 correct — identical answers to the scout's thinking-ON run

headline.verdict: mainC's DIRECTION is confirmed and its MAGNITUDE is not. Production gemma (thinking off) answers all five prompts in 2.97 s vs LFM2.5's 12.89 s — 4.3x faster, not ~31x. Thinking ON, gemma takes 48.18 s — 3.7x SLOWER than LFM. The per-token decode advantage LFM holds (2.08x measured here) is real but is swamped by the ~15x token-count difference the toggle creates.
headline.what_was_wrong_with_the_inferred_number: the chars/4 proxy undercounted gemma's thinking-ON emission (902 measured vs ~599 inferred) and LFM's (501 measured vs ~398 inferred), and the ~0.3 s figure for production gemma applied a rate near LFM's to gemma's tokens. Measured answer emission is 6.6 tokens/prompt (not ~12) but gemma decodes at 19.4 t/s (not ~40), and per-call prefill on a 26B MoE costs ~0.26 s — so 2.97 s, not 0.3 s.

artifacts.raw: gen_*.out / gen_*.err (stderr carries common_perf_print and the --verbose-prompt token dump)
